title: Exploring the pharmacokinetic, toxicity and anti-arthritic activity of bioactive polyphenols to mitigate the HIF-regulated angiogenic-pannus growth in rheumatoid arthritis.
authors: Kalidass, Bharathi; Nazeer, Abdul Azeez; Mahalingam, Malathi; Raja, Ramalingam Karthik; Lakshmanan, Dinesh Kumar
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦类风湿关节炎中多酚类化合物的药代动力学、毒性和抗炎活性，涉及分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Current therapies for rheumatoid arthritis, including anti-inflammatory agents and immunomodulators, primarily target common inflammatory mechanisms. However, the efficacy of most bioactive compounds claimed to possess anti-arthritic properties remains mechanistically unproven, particularly against progressive conditions like pannus development. This study investigates the pharmacokinetics, toxicity, and impact of reported anti-arthritic polyphenols on HIF-regulated pannus development in rheumatoid arthritis through in silico and in vitro approaches. Eighty bioactive compounds with documented anti-arthritic properties were selected from the literature and subjected to sequential evaluation of pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic activity. The study identified five promising candidates qualified to perform in vivo toxicity and in vitro biochemical assays. Toxicity testing using Galleria mellonella larvae indicated dose-dependent effects on the midgut, with no mortality observed at doses up to 2000 mg/kg body weight. In vitro assays, including antioxidant and anti-inflammatory evaluations, further validated the therapeutic potential of these compounds. Compounds that satisfied all predictive criteria were subjected to molecular interaction analysis against hub-gene targets implicated in HIF-regulated angiogenesis in rheumatoid arthritis. RA-associated proteins were identified from NCBI-GEO and DisGeNET (GWAS) databases. Functional annotation and protein-protein interaction analysis identified IL-6, IL-1beta, HIF-1alpha, PPARG, and TIMP1 as key hub targets. Molecular docking using PyRx revealed the binding affinities of the selected bioactive compounds against these targets. These findings suggest that the screened bioactive polyphenols exhibit low toxicity and hold potential as regulators of HIF-mediated angiogenesis in rheumatoid arthritis, offering a novel therapeutic approach for progressive disease management.
abstract_zh: 类风湿关节炎的现行疗法，包括抗炎药和免疫调节剂，主要针对常见的炎症机制。然而，大多数声称具有抗关节炎特性的生物活性化合物的疗效在机制上仍未得到证实，尤其是在进行性疾病如血管翳形成方面。本研究通过计算机模拟和体外实验方法，探讨了已报道的抗关节炎多酚类化合物在类风湿关节炎中对HIF调控的血管翳形成的药代动力学、毒性及影响。从文献中选取了80种具有记录抗关节炎特性的生物活性化合物，并对其进行了药效学和药代动力学活性的序贯评估。研究确定了五种有前景的候选化合物，符合进行体内毒性和体外生化检测的条件。使用大蜡螟幼虫进行的毒性测试显示，对中肠有剂量依赖性影响，在高达2000 mg/kg体重的剂量下未观察到死亡。体外实验，包括抗氧化和抗炎评估，进一步验证了这些化合物的治疗潜力。满足所有预测标准的化合物被用于与类风湿关节炎中HIF调控血管生成相关的枢纽基因靶点的分子相互作用分析。从NCBI-GEO和DisGeNET（GWAS）数据库中鉴定了类风湿关节炎相关蛋白。功能注释和蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用分析确定了IL-6、IL-1β、HIF-1α、PPARG和TIMP1为关键枢纽靶点。使用PyRx进行的分子对接揭示了所选生物活性化合物对这些靶点的结合亲和力。这些发现表明，筛选出的生物活性多酚类化合物表现出低毒性，并具有作为类风湿关节炎中HIF介导血管生成调节剂的潜力，为进行性疾病管理提供了一种新的治疗途径。
